stem: Diabetes mellitus occurs when which measured quantity is too high?

options.label: A
options.text: Blood glucose concentration above the healthy range
options.misconception: Recognizes the source-defined abnormality: excessive blood glucose.
options.explanation: The source defines diabetes as occurring when blood glucose, also called blood sugar, is too high.

options.label: B
options.text: Arterial blood pressure above the healthy range
options.misconception: Confuses diabetes with a disorder defined by arterial pressure.
options.explanation: Arterial pressure is a different measurement; it is not the high blood glucose stated in the definition.

options.label: C
options.text: Blood oxygen concentration above the healthy range
options.misconception: Confuses glucose metabolism with oxygen transport.
options.explanation: Blood oxygen describes gas transport rather than the blood glucose abnormality named by the source.

options.label: D
options.text: Urinary protein excretion above the healthy range
options.misconception: Confuses the defining abnormality with a renal measurement.
options.explanation: Protein excretion is a different measurement; it is not the high blood glucose that defines diabetes here.

options.label: E
options.text: Blood sodium concentration above the healthy range
options.misconception: Confuses blood sugar with an unrelated serum electrolyte.
options.explanation: Sodium is an electrolyte measurement, whereas the cited definition identifies excessive blood glucose.

context: Learning objective: distinguish the defining diabetes measurement. Glucose circulates as blood sugar and is a major energy source; diabetes mellitus is the condition in which blood glucose becomes too high.
imageCaption: Insulin lowers circulating glucose by promoting storage; glucagon mobilizes fuel during fasting.
